The function defined in (1) is a rather special example of an extremely important class of functions, the polynomial functions. A function f is a polynomial
function if there are real numbers ao, ... , an such that
f(x) = anx" + an_\x + • • • + aix + a\x + ao, for all x
(when f(x) is written in this form it is usually tacitly assumed that an / 0). The
highest power of x with a nonzero coefficient is called the degree of f; for
example, the polynomial function f defined by f(x) = 5x6 + 137x4 — n has
degree 6.
